messages.subject: geom_point and position_dodge
parts:
I think the action of position_dodge when applied to geom_point has
changed. Consider the following example:

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=factor(cyl), y=mpg, colour=factor(am))) +
geom_boxplot()
p
p + geom_point()
p + geom_point(position=position_dodge(width=0.5))

Previously, I thought (though of course I can not find an example),
that this would dodge the groups of points (as normally defined; here
the interaction of factor(cyl) and factor(am)) together, giving the
red points all aligned vertically with the bar of the box plot
(assuming the correct width was defined). Now it dodges each
individual point separately, spreading them across the given width.

I can get the effect I am going for with

p + geom_point(aes(x=as.numeric(factor(cyl)) +
0.375*as.numeric(factor(am)) - 1.5*0.375))

but that seems rather hackish. Did this behavior change? If so, why,
and could it change back, or could there be a way to have the dodging
work only at the grouping level instead of the individual element
level?

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: geom_point and position_dodge
parts:
Hi Brian,

I'm pretty that dodge has always acted this way with points, mainly
because position_dodge works with individual elements, rather than
groups. I'm not sure if it would be possible to work at the group
level for points and still get the behaviour you'd expect for other
geoms.

Hadley
